reasoning: Reproduced live on a standalone local session (status bar shows 'Local', no pairing). Settings > Location renders the 'Sync from Server / Fetch location from Headless Server' row enabled — location_settings.dart reads isRemoteMode at :103 but only uses it at :354, so this row is NOT gated. Clicking it produces the green snackbar 'Location synced from server' (captured at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/r7band.png; it takes ~4s to appear under softpipe, which is why an earlier fast capture missed it). The native log proves nothing was fetched: every click emits '[API] api_set_location called with lat=0, lon=0, elev=0' — the handler read this app's own location (0/0/0) back out of profileSettingsBackendProvider and wrote the identical values straight back. Six clicks, six identical log lines. Location cited (:182-232) matches the row, which spans :181-235.

title: Importing a detailed .hor horizon silently collapses it to 8 sector maxima — a single tree blocks a whole 45-degree sector
reasoning: Confirmed in source, which is decisive here. HorizonProfile.parseHorizonText (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/settings_provider.dart:567-603) parses every sample, then hands them to HorizonProfile.fromSamples (:539-555), which rounds each azimuth to one of 8 45-degree sectors (index = floor(((az+22.5)%360)/45)%8) and keeps only `if (alt > altitudes[dir]) altitudes[dir] = alt` — the per-sector MAXIMUM, discarding every other sample. location_settings.dart:497-501 documents the reduction ('highest altitude per sector wins so an obstruction is never under-reported') and :526 shows the only user-facing message: 'Horizon profile imported from <file>' — no sample count, no mention of the reduction. Severity lowered to P3 because the app's horizon model is 8-sector everywhere (horizonDirections), so the reduction is intrinsic and conservative; the shippable defect is the silence about it, not a wrong number. Did not drive the native file-picker; the source path is unambiguous and the reported 8 values are consistent with per-sector maxima.

The path half is FIXED: backup_service.dart:1051-1055 _getBackupDirectory now calls the new resolveDefaultBackupDirectory() (:135-145), which resolves 'backups/' beside resolveDefaultDatabaseFile(environment) and therefore honours SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR. The disclosure half still reproduces: AutoSaveConfig defaults are backupEnabled=true, backupInterval=24h, maxBackups=7 (auto_save_service.dart:26-33), and the Status section (auto_save_settings.dart:306-372) renders only 'Last backup', 'Last error' and a 'Back Up Now' button — it never names the directory and offers no way to change it, while 'Maximum backups' prunes files in that unnamed folder. Severity dropped to P3 now that the cross-install/undeclared-volume leak is gone.

title: The session checkpoint lives outside the database, so the app offers to resume a sequence its own database has never heard of — and the failure dialog contradicts itself
reasoning: Reproduced deliberately, without relying on the report's concurrent-instance accident. I pointed XDG_DATA_HOME at /tmp/ns-audit/v2sg-xdg (so getApplicationSupportDirectory resolves there) and planted one checkpoint at .../com.skotiq.desktop/skotiq_session.checkpoint with is_active=true, executor_state=Running, completed_exposures=4, completed_integration_secs=1200. SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR still pointed at the profile's own database, whose sequences / sequence_nodes / sequence_runs / captured_images tables all held 0 rows. On launch the app showed 'Recover Sequence? ... Sequence: New Sequence / Saved: 0m ago / Completed: 4 frames (20m integration)' — /tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/60b-recover.png. That proves the mechanism: app_shell.dart:346-348 sets the checkpoint dir to getApplicationSupportDirectory(), which ignores SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR and SKOTIQ_DATABASE_DIR entirely, and the dialog's frame count comes from the checkpoint file (app_shell.dart:432-436), not from the database. WORSE THAN REPORTED: pressing Resume did not merely prompt — it STARTED THE RUN (executor went Running 'New Sequence', then Recovery started / DeviceDisconnected attempt 1/9) against a sequence tree the database has never seen (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2sg/61-fail-s.png). The self-contradiction half is confirmed in source but was not live-triggered here, because my planted checkpoint was genuinely resumable: app_shell.dart:437-446 composes, unconditionally whenever resume throws, SkotiqAlert(title:'Recovery did not complete', message: '$lastError\n\nThe checkpoint is still available. Retry resume or discard it to start fresh.'), and lastError is the raw caught object (runAppCheckpointRecovery, app_shell.dart:60-83), so a Dart Exception renders verbatim as 'Exception: No valid checkpoint to resume from' (sequence_executor.dart:1722) right above a sentence asserting the checkpoint is still available. Location app_shell.dart:398 for the dialog title is exact.
